thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Lower as US-Saudi Arabia Tensions Weigh on Sentiment; Street Digests Bank Earnings

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Lower as US-Saudi Arabia Tensions Weigh on Sentiment; Street Digests Bank Earnings
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Monday's regular session:
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.1%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.2%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.8%
iPath S&P 500 VIX ST Futures ETN ( VXX ): +2.2%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -0.3%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was off 0.3%.
US stock futures were pointing to a negative opening, as Wall Street digested Q3 earnings from major financial firms Bank of America (BAC) and Charles Schwab (SCHW).
Geopolitical issues have also weighed on market sentiment, particularly the brewing tensions between the US and Saudi Arabia stemming from the disappearance of Washington Post columnist Jamal Khashoggi. US President Donald Trump has vowed to punish Saudi Arabia if proven the country is involved in the disappearance, while the MIddle Eastern country has in turn threatened to retaliate. Consequently, crude oil prices have rallied.
In economic data news, retail sales rose 0.1% in September -- the second month in a row -- versus expectations for an increase of 0.6%.
Meanwhile, the Empire State Index, which tracks manufacturing in New York, showed an increase of 2.1 points to a 21.1 reading in October, versus forecasts for a reading of 20.
Power Play: Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were flat.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was up 0.2% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were inactive in pre-market trade.
Sears Holdings (SHLD) plunged more than 26% after the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and will close 142 stores by the end of the year in addition to the 46 already slated to be shut. Chief Executive Edward Lampert has stepped down from his role, effective immediately, but will remain chairman of the company's board. Sears has received commitments for $300 million in senior priming debtor-in-possession financial from lenders and is working toward another $300 million subordinated DIP financing with ESL Investments, the company's largest stockholder and creditor. Lampert is ESL's chairman and CEO. The funding will support operations during the restructuring process. The company said in a statement it plans to continue paying employees' wages and benefits and vendors while honoring member programs. Sears and Kmart stores and their online and mobile platforms will continue to operate and holding services and brand business will continue to operate as usual.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.2%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 0.2% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 1.2%.
Bank of America (BAC) rose marginally after it reported Q3 earnings of $0.66 per share, up from $0.46 in the same period a year ago and exceeding the estimate of $0.62 from analysts polled by Capital IQ. Total revenue of $22.78 billion was up from $21.84 billion in the same period a year ago and topped the Street projection of $22.63 billion.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 0.8% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were flat.
Apple (AAPL) was down marginally after it acquired Asaii, a startup that developed a music analytics engine for artist managers and music labels, Axios said on Sunday, citing a source close to the matter. The source added that the deal was worth less than $100 million.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) were both inactive in the pre-market session.
Nine Energy Service (NINE) disclosed that it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Magnum Oil Tools International, a downhole technology provider serving the global oil and gas industry for over a decade. Total upfront deal of $493 million consists of a combination of about $334 million of cash, as well as 5 million shares of Nine common stock, which is valued at $159 million, based on a 30-day value-weighted average price as of Oct. 12. The terms include the potential for additional future contingent payments, according to a statement. Magnum does not have any debt, it added. The company intends to fund the cash purchase price with the net proceeds of a debt sale announced concurrently with the acquisition, borrowings under a new credit facility, and cash on hand. The firm said in a separate statement early Monday that it intends to offer $400 million of senior unsecured notes due 2023 in a private placement.
Commodities
Crude was up 0.8%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 0.5%. Natural gas was up 2.7% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 2.8%.
Gold was down 0.1%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 1%. Silver was up 1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.8%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.1% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were quiet. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 0.8%.
Tandem Diabetes Care (TNDM) rose more than 5% after it said it has received a Heath Canada medical device license for the t:slim X2 insulin pump. The company said the device is the only continuous glucose monitoring insulin pump approved in Canada for daily diabetes treatment without fingersticks. Tandem plans to launch the t:slim X2 on a province-by-province basis throughout Q4.
